relevance_note: The review describes one identifiable person with an HA20 diagnosis and a clinical feature, "a patient treated for longstanding intestinal BD-like symptoms was later diagnosed with A20 haploinsufficiency [91]", so an in-scope individual with individual-level detail exists.
method_note: This is a narrative review (no cohort of its own). I read the whole file, including the reference list and all tables. Only one person has individual-level detail: the patient attributed to reference [91]; applying the v4 rule (a passing mention is in scope when it gives sex, age, variant or a feature), this person's longstanding intestinal BD-like symptoms count as a feature, so one individual row was created with label 'ref [91] patient' and source_reference_in_review '[91]'. All other HA20 mentions are group-level only (five families [13]; 16 patients [41]; 11 paediatric cases of monogenic mimics [33]) and got no rows; Table 3 gives disease-level symbols for HA 20, not patients, so no table symbols or stacked cells needed interpretation. The paper prints no TNFAIP3 variant description for this person, so the variants row keeps variant_original_string 'not reported'. No contradictions between statements were found. The person's country/ethnicity was not taken from the title of reference [91] ('a Chinese Patient'), because the paper does not state it in its own text about the person.
